title: Portfolio-First Interview Playbook + 90d Activation
content:
Purpose and scope
- Quick experiment doc for shifting mid-senior IC hiring to a portfolio-first loop. Goal: surface real impact, reduce takehome testing, shorten time-to-offer.
- Scope: IC3-IC5 engineering tracks, product-design pairings optional. Pilot 8 roles over Q1 2026.

Hypotheses
1) Portfolio-first interviews increase quality signal for ownership and impact vs pure takehome tests.
2) Candidates are more likely to accept offers when first-week onboarding plan is visible during loop.
3) Interviewer time per hire will decrease by 10% after streamlining scoring into a single rubric.

Roles and responsibilities
- Hiring manager: defines portfolio prompt areas and shortlists artifacts.
- Recruiter: screens for baseline, sends portfolio guidance, owns calendar.
- Interviewer lead: calibrates rubric, runs 1 calibration session per role.
- People ops: run experiment, collect feedback, iterate.

Interview loop (compact)
1) Recruiter screen (30m) - culture fit, timeline, comp expectations, role clarifying questions.
2) Portfolio submission (candidate chooses up to 3 artifacts, 1 paged summary) - not mandatory to be code only.
3) Portfolio deep-dive (60m) - candidate walks through 2 artifacts, emphasis on tradeoffs, metrics, postmortems, what they would change.
4) System/architecture or design pairing (45-60m) - focused on a product slice related to portfolio. Could be whiteboard or Mural.
5) Execution/owner interview (45m) - timeline, prioritization, ambiguous project decomposition, dependency handling.
6) Debrief sync (15-30m) - interviewer lead consolidates scores before hiring manager discussion.

Scoring rubric (single sheet, 1-5 scale where 3=meets bar)
- Technical depth: evidence of mastery and teachability. Notes: evaluate complexity of implemented systems, not lines of code.
- Product impact: did artifacts move metrics, customers, or reduce cost? concrete signals.
- Ownership & execution: end-to-end delivery, ambiguity handling, cross-team coordination.
- Communication & mentorship: clarity in storytelling, code reviews, docs.
- Tradeoff judgement: ability to balance speed, quality, maintainability.
- Culture add & collaboration: alignment with Redwood values and team norms.
Guidance: 1=severe gaps, 2=some gaps, 3=solid contributor, 4=strong, 5=exceptional leader for level.

Rubric quick form (example)
Candidate: __________ Role: __________  Date: __________
Technical depth: 4
Product impact: 3
Ownership: 4
Communication: 3
Tradeoffs: 4
Culture: 3
Overall recommendation: hire/hold/no-hire  Notes: short bullet bullets with examples e.g., 'led migration from X -> Y reduced latency 42%'

Calibration notes (to run before 1st panel)
- Bring 3 recorded sample rubrics from previous hires (anonymized).
- Run a 45m calibration session with 4 interviewers, aim for 80% alignment on overall hire/hold.
- Save one candidate as calibration artifact for future panels.

Communication templates (recruiter)
- Portfolio guidance note: 3 bullets on what we want, 1 pager template, examples. Keep it optional but encouraged.
- Interview prep note: first week snapshot, manager intro, primary projects, onboarding buddy assignment. Attach to interview invite.

Onboarding 90-day activation checklist (manager + ops)
- Before Day 1: equipment order confirmed, access to repo and infra requested, 30/60/90 goals drafted and sent.
- Day 1: Welcome, paperwork, team standup intro, 1:1 with manager, pair with buddy on small read-only task.
- Week 1: Rotate through product demos, join onboarding cohort lunch, hands-on ticket to run dev workflow, security playbook read.
- Week 2-4: 1st small owner task with clear acceptance criteria, initial feedback loop established, infra ramp checklist completed.
- Month 2: own a minor feature, present impact plan to team, career conversation with manager about expectations.
- Month 3: deliver first independent piece of work, retro on onboarding, update 30/60/90 and set next milestone.

Manager playbook for first 30 days (short bullets)
- Day 0: confirm systems access, add to team calendar, assign mentor.
- Day 1: set 1:1 cadence weekly, share top 3 priorities, set expectations on async communication.
- Week 2: give small project with measurable outcome; check-in mid-week.
- Week 4: 30-day check with written feedback and updated goals.

Experiment measurement & success criteria
- Reduce time-to-offer from screening to offer by 15% compared to baseline.
- Candidate acceptance rate >= baseline or improves by 5%.
- Hiring manager satisfaction score >= 4/5 in post-hire survey.
- Interviewer time per candidate decreases by 10% after rubric consolidation.

Open questions & risks
- Some roles will need code tests for regulatory or safety reasons; define exceptions.
- Portfolio variance: how to compare different artifact types fairly. Proposed: normalize by impact statement and scope.
- Bias risk: portfolios favor folks with previous product access. Mitigation: recruiters coach on framing and allow alternative evidence.

Next steps / timeline
- Jan week 2: finalize rubric and recruiter templates.
- Jan week 3: run 2 calibration sessions.
- Feb: pilot begins with up to 8 roles. Weekly check-ins with hiring managers.
- Mar: analyze metrics and iterate.

Notes to self and followups
- Connect with applied-ml hiring lead for cross-discipline calibration.
- Draft one-pager explainer for hiring managers that can be attached to reqs.
- Prepare anonymized rubric examples to add to shared folder.

References and templates attached/linked
- 1 page portfolio guidance template (attached under recruiting-templates).
- Example rubric anonymized.
- First-week onboarding template for managers.
